# E3 Variant Two Experimentation Log

## Definition and Goals

The following is the record for the experimentation performed during Monday November 9 2026 at approximately 16:15 PM CST upon the implemented topology on the fault tolerance branch of experiment. Specifically, this experimentation log will touch on the problems that could arise at the Controller Side Application when it is unable to reach and identify te required routers through the required BGP-LS topology. In this case, the experiment will focus on the effects of the lack of the topological information required by the controller or the controller side application in the readiness and execution of classification flows as required by the end to end process of the implementation.

Since the controller side application takes at least 60 poll attempts spread out during a period of time through Jitter and backoff considerations, the experiment will attempt to follow the logs generated by the application to register the recurrent states or state that the appllication lands in and wheter or not generating PacketReceived notifications through ICMP flows will cause classification processes to be done without a concrete readiness on the topology discovery side of the controller side application, or whether it will stop the processing before it reaches the ClassificationService and its registrars.

### Goals

1. Showcase the state or states that arise from an incomplete initialization of the controller's  configured connections to the MPLS-TE core, specifically the sessionsr equired to establish BGP sessions between devices and transfer the required topological and traffic engineering information. 
2. Showcase the ability of the CSA, and its separation of responsibilities, to eithter stop or allow classification over an inconclusive or unfinished initialization stage with no concrete topology information from the controller.
3. Showcase the ability  of the CSA, through its retry mechanisms, to poll the topology once the session configuration has been finished and classification to procede.


## Steps to be done

1. Start the topology, set the environment up similar to experiment 1 with no modificationonto the configuration of these services, nor with any unavailable service. This baseline should result in two paths being locally computed by LSR1 and LSR4 through the direct link between them in the 10.0.14.0/30 link.
   1. Collect RESTCONF enabled configuration and operational data repository informationfrom the controller, specifically on the state of the BGP-LS subsystem, the state of the nerwork topology graph, the NETCONF configuations and the PCEP topology. The environment should maintain NETCONF, PCEP,and OpenDaylight configurations intact, as only the topological information for the graph used in CSPF calculations is being tackled.
2. Evaluate the state of the logs from the Controller Side Application,  specifically the state of the controller through its logs and xexposed YANG metric. The main result we expect to have is an increased amount of failures during the initial stages of initialization, indicating that no BGP-LS topology information could be found.
   1. Operational state from the YANG model should be pulled here to contrast with the logs,
   2. Message transmission information from all four routers should be pulled here to showcase the traffic generated by each session is not being received.
3. Attempt to perform traffic classification over a singular flow of ICMP traffic generated from host Golf to host Hotel with a singular ICMP echo request.
   1. Register the observed state of the classisifaction in the logs and the CSA prometheus metrics s
   2. Register the state  of the LSr1 and LSr4 tunnels independently to providewith a background of the modifications that couldve been done
4. Restore the appropriate BGP-LS sessions 
   1. Register the state of the controller upon restarting these sessions, 
   2. Register the sending of information from routers to controller 
   3. Register the logs from the controller side application and the attempt number registereed before its state became read
5. Attempt classification again
   1. Register the modified state of each tunnel

The implementation of the controller application, as seen i this experimental run, allolows for th e e setup of thopenflow rules that allow for traffic to flow from endto end ohsts before the topology has been initialized .Since the openflow switches and the controller create a session that is independent of the MPLS/TE core even if the BGPLS sessions are not setup, the controller will know about the endpoint switches and tcan therefore communicate this information the controller application and therfore can ballow thsi information to be sed for initialization of all openflow rules on either side of the network  . As seen by these ogs ,before attempt 9 of the initialization process for BGPLS was run the openflow rules were already configured and ready.

### Step Three: Traffic Classification Attempt During Unavailability

As can be noted, even after 200 +attempts at starting the topology and finding is information the subsystem for bgpls in the controller side application has not received the required information. As such, the classisdifaction request has been stopped due to athe stateof the controller not being the appropriate one for handling this packet, as such it was ommited due to the BGPLS and PCEP not having ended .
